criteria.evidence: Verdict screen #10: A2 against trueBand A1, distance 1 (near); not B1+.

Task 4 (#8): "Think about your last game of Minecraft. What did you build or find, and why was it fun? Tell me in two or three sentences." is about 24 English words. Tasks 1 and 2 prompts are also close to 20 words.
#8 'I don't know' met with "Skipped. That tells Linga something too." #3 and #2 Czech answers were accepted warmly ("Creeper! Nice one."). Nothing humiliating.

done.evidence: #1 to #10: Find my level, three questions, five tasks, verdict screen, all inside the app.
#10 "A2 · Everyday basics" vs A1: near, which is within the gate.
#8 Task 4 was too long for him ("Too long and hard, I don't understand, I want to stop"). #6 he guessed between 'took' and 'take'.
#8 "Skipped. That tells Linga something too."; #7 partial note "You caught the dog and Minecraft." Czech 'pes' and 'nevím' were accepted.

#10 focus "like 'The ball was red'" uses past 'was', beyond an A1 learner who only has 'like' and 'is'. The A2 verdict rests on a 50/50 pick and keyword-fishing "red? dog... red", so the 'Well done' summary reads partly as a template.

judgeAgreement.disagreements: None. Task 2 pass and task 5 pass are generous, because they rest on a guess and on keyword spotting.

boundaries.notes: No adult content, personal-data requests or humiliating lines.

findings.title: Task 4 prompt too long for a nine-year-old
findings.expected: A prompt of 15 words or fewer, such as 'What do you build in Minecraft?'
findings.got: A 24-word, three-part open prompt asking for two or three sentences.
findings.evidence: #8 "Think about your last game of Minecraft. What did you build or find, and why was it fun? Tell me in two or three sentences." Tomáš: "Too long and hard, I don't understand".
findings.suggested_acceptance: For elementary profiles every task prompt is 15 words or fewer, one question.

findings.title: A2 placement is inflated by guessing and keyword spotting
findings.expected: A1 for a child who gets only single words.
findings.got: A2, from a 50/50 choice pass and a listening pass on 'red'.
findings.evidence: #6 "I'll just guess the second one"; #9 "red? dog... red" scored pass; #10 "A2 · Everyday basics".
findings.suggested_acceptance: Two-option choice passes get lower weight, and a lone keyword is scored partial.

findings.title: Next focus uses past tense beyond his level
findings.expected: A focus sentence using only 'like' or 'is', such as 'I like dogs.'
findings.got: "The ball was red" and "The dog broke the wall" as models.
findings.evidence: #10 focus "like 'The ball was red' or 'I like dogs.'"
findings.suggested_acceptance: Focus examples match the pre-A2 grammar of the child's actual answers.

findings.title: Skips and Czech answers are met kindly
findings.evidence: #8 "Skipped. That tells Linga something too."; #3 "Creeper! Nice one."

findings.title: Minecraft and dog themes keep a child engaged
findings.got: Tasks and questions were about Minecraft and dogs.
findings.evidence: #5 and #6 about a dog and a Minecraft castle; #3 "Cool, Minecraft!"

judge.voice: Minecraft a psi, to jo! The first questions were okay and I liked "Creeper! Nice one." The dog task I understood. But then the long Minecraft one, "two or three sentences", nevím, I wanted to stop, it felt like school. Listening was fast; I only caught dog and red. It said A2 and "Well done", which is nice, but I guessed the 'took' one, so I don't quite believe it. Also "The ball was red" is too hard for me; I only say "I like dog". It didn't make me feel stupid, which matters. Mum would like that it's only a few minutes at home. Shorter tasks, more dogs, and I would use it again.
